messages:
Kai (Design): quick design review: sharing two directions for the Prompt Sets results — 'row compression' (denser list with inline metadata) vs 'card scaffolding' (separated tiles). thinking about scanline keyboard nav, approval affordance, and regression-diff anchors. link: https://figma.redwood/xyz

Marta (Product): thanks! main Q: which preserves clarity for scorecards & quick approvals? we get frequent asks to 'approve next' without opening detail panel. also need a visible undo affordance for accidental approves.

Sam (Eng): impl notes: row compression is much cheaper — single list render, only expands preview on demand. cards need more DOM and might impact rerender for huge runs (10k). both can reuse existing virtualized list though.

Jenny (DevEx): copy nit: approval CTA should be clear about what it does. instead of 'Approve' maybe 'Approve run (mark as pass)' to avoid confusion. also propose small toast: 'Run approved — undo' rather than destructive modal.

Alex (Accessibility): a11y nits: whichever pattern we pick we must ensure a) focus order doesn't skip scorecard details b) keyboard shortcut for approve has an accessible label and confirmation state c) toast must be announced by screen readers with role=alert. row compression might collapse context — make sure truncation has an expand control with aria-controls.

Kai (Design): noted. mockups include a subtle focus halo and an expand chevron that is keyboard reachable. For card scaffolding I added a persistent approve button in top-right of each card; for row compression the approve control is a right-aligned icon button revealed on hover/focus.

Marta (Product): tradeoffs: card makes approval explicit but increases scan time for reviewers; row is denser for power users. Can we offer a user-level density toggle in the runs view and a per-team default?

Sam (Eng): density toggle is straightforward if we keep the same data model — two CSS/display modes. per-team default requires backend flag (small), but we can default to user's last choice initially.

Jenny (DevEx): UX flow for bulk approvals: if multiple selected, show a confirmation strip with 'Approve selected (n)' and 'Undo' toast. Also propose keyboard 'Shift+A' to approve selected.

Alex (Accessibility): bulk approve must have an opt-in accessible confirmation (aria-modal or clear inline confirmation) to avoid accidental mass actions for screen reader users. Also announce selection count.

Sam (Eng): quick feasibility: I can prototype row-mode + density toggle in the next sprint. Card layout would need more CSS effort and perf testing. ETA: row + toggle prototype in 2 weeks.

Kai (Design): microcopy proposals (small):
- approve button: "Approve run"
- undo toast: "Run approved — undo"
- bulk CTA: "Approve selected (n)"
- compact tooltip for truncated prompt: "Show full prompt"

Marta (Product): love those. one more: when a regression diff is present, add a small red badge "regressions" next to scorecard so reviewers don't miss it.

Alex (Accessibility): badge should include text not only color: "Regressions: 3" to be keyboard readable. Also ensure color contrast meets AA.

Sam (Eng): noted. badges are easy. final question: do we need per-run scorecard inline or just on hover/expand?

Kai (Design): inline mini-score (2–3 metrics) in row-mode, full scorecard on expand. cards get mini-score in header. keeps scanline quick.

Jenny (DevEx): will add docs for keyboard shortcuts and an accessibility note in the prompt-sets guide. Also re: analytics, track 'approved-via-keyboard' vs 'approved-via-click' — helps understand power-user adoption.

Marta (Product): plan: go with row compression + density toggle + undo toast + accessible badges. Sam to prototype, Kai to iterate mocks, Alex to review a11y when prototype is ready. Thanks everyone. :tada:

ui-ci-bot: deploy preview available at https://staging.redwood/run-views/2329001111 — share feedback by EOD on Thursday.
